all the valiant men arose and took away the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the oak{e} in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
So Saul died for his unfaithfulness that he committed against Yahweh, because he did not keep the word of Yahweh, and also because he consulted a medium, seeking guidance,{f}
and did not seek guidance from Yahweh. Therefore he put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.{g}

notes.text: Verses 1–12 parallel 1 Samuel 31:1–13. Philistines, a people of the coast, perhaps “wanderers”; Gilboa, perhaps “bubbling spring.”

First Samuel 31:6 reads “his armor-bearer and all his men died together that day.” Chronicles makes the end of Saul’s dynasty explicit, though a son, Esh-baal (Ish-bosheth), survived (8:33; 2 Samuel 2:8).
First Samuel 31:10 says they put his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan. Dagon was a grain or fish god of the Philistines.
Jabesh-gilead, “dry place of Gilead.”
First Samuel 31:13 reads “under the tamarisk tree.” Chronicles also omits the burning of the bodies (1 Samuel 31:12).
See 1 Samuel 13:13–14; 15:22–23; 28:6–19. Verses 13–14 have no parallel in Samuel. Saul is said not to have sought Yahweh, though 1 Samuel 28:6 says Yahweh did not answer him.
David, see 2:15; Jesse, see 2:12.

verses.text: Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.{a}

In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led Israel out and brought them in. And Yahweh your God said to you, ‘You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be prince over my people Israel.’”

So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before Yahweh. And they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of Yahweh by Samuel.{b}
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were.{c}
The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here.” Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David.{d}
David said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall be chief and commander.” Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became chief.{e}
David dwelt in the stronghold; for this reason they called it the city of David.
He built the city all around, from the Millo to the surrounding wall; and Joab repaired the rest of the city.{f}
And David became greater and greater, for Yahweh of Armies was with him.{g}
These are the chiefs of David’s mighty men, who strongly supported him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of Yahweh concerning Israel.{h}
This is the list of David’s mighty men: Jashobeam, a Hachmonite, chief of the thirty;{i} he lifted up his spear against three hundred whom he killed at one time.{j}
After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite; he was one of the three mighty men.{k}
He was with David at Pas-dammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where was a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.{l}
But they took their stand in the middle of the plot and defended it, and struck down the Philistines; and Yahweh saved them by a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to David, to the cave of Adullam, while the army of the Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.{m}
David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.
David longed and said, “Oh that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!”

Then the three broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to David. But David would not drink it; he poured it out to Yahweh

and said, “Far be it from me before my God that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy? For at the risk of their lives they brought it.” Therefore he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the three.{n} He lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them, and won a name beside the three.
Of the three he was more honored than the two,{o} and he was made their captain; however, he did not attain to the first three.
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a valiant man of Kabzeel, great in deeds, struck down two sons of Ariel{p} of Moab. He also went down and struck a lion in a pit on a day when snow had fallen.{q}

And he struck down an Egyptian, a man of great stature, seven and a half feet tall.{r} In the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
These things Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did, and won a name beside the three mighty men.
He was honored among the thirty, but he did not attain to the three. And David set him over his bodyguard.
The mighty men of the armies were Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,{s}
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,{t}
Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,{u}
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,{v}
Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite,{w}
Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,{x}
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,{y}
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,{z}
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite,{aa}
Ahiam son of Sachar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,{ab}
Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,{ac}
Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai,{ad}
Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri,{ae}
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor-bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,{af}
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,{ag}
Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai,{ah}
Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,{ai}
Hanan the son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,{aj}
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,{ak}
Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,{al}
Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,{am}
Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.{an}

notes.text: Verses 1–9 parallel 2 Samuel 5:1–10. Chronicles omits David’s seven years as king over Judah alone (2 Samuel 2–4).
See 1 Samuel 16:1–13.
Jebus, perhaps “trodden down”; compare 1:14. Second Samuel 5:6 says “the king and his men.”
Zion, perhaps “fortress” or “dry place.” Chronicles omits the saying about the blind and the lame (2 Samuel 5:6, 8).
Second Samuel 5:8 does not name Joab here. Joab, see 2:16.
Millo means “filling,” probably a terrace or earthwork.
Hebrew Yahweh Tseba’oth, often rendered “Yahweh of hosts”: Yahweh as commander of the armies of heaven and of Israel. This is its first appearance in this book.
Verses 10–41 parallel 2 Samuel 23:8–39; verses 41b–47 are found only in Chronicles.

So the written Hebrew text (Ketiv) and the Septuagint; the Hebrew margin (Qere) reads “the officers.” Second Samuel 23:8 calls him Josheb-basshebeth (perhaps a scribal change of Ish-baal) and “chief of the three.” Jashobeam, “the people will return”; Hachmonite, “wise.”
Second Samuel 23:8 reads “eight hundred.” The Septuagint (B text) here also reads “three hundred.”
Eleazar, see 6:3; Dodo, “his beloved”; Ahohite, of Ahoah (8:4).

Pas-dammim (1 Samuel 17:1 Ephes-dammim), “boundary of blood.” Here Chronicles passes from Eleazar’s deed to that of Shammah (2 Samuel 23:11–12), apparently because a line dropped out; in Samuel the field was full of lentils.
Or “Three of the thirty, the chiefs”; 2 Samuel 23:13. Adullam, perhaps “refuge”; Rephaim, “ghosts” or “giants.”
So the Hebrew; the Syriac reads “the thirty” (also in verse 21 and 2 Samuel 23:18). Abishai, see 2:16.
Or “Of the three he was doubly honored.”
Ariel, “lion of God”; Hebrew “two Ariel of Moab,” perhaps meaning “two champions.”
Benaiah, see 4:36; Jehoiada, “Yahweh knows”; Kabzeel, “God gathers.”
Hebrew “five cubits” (about 2.3 meters). Second Samuel 23:21 does not give his height.
Elhanan, “God is gracious”; Asahel, see 2:16.

Second Samuel 23:25 reads “Shammah the Harodite” and adds “Elika the Harodite.” Shammoth, “desolations”; Harorite, perhaps from Harod (“trembling”); Helez, see 2:39; Pelonite, uncertain (2 Samuel 23:26 Paltite).
Ira, “watchful”; Ikkesh, “perverse”; Tekoite, of Tekoa (2:24); Abiezer, see 7:18; Anathothite, of Anathoth (6:60).
Sibbecai (2 Samuel 23:27 Mebunnai), perhaps “Yahweh has interwoven”; Hushathite, of Hushah (4:4); Ilai (2 Samuel 23:28 Zalmon), uncertain.
Maharai, “hasty”; Heled (2 Samuel 23:29 Heleb), “duration”; Baanah, perhaps “son of affliction.”
Ithai (2 Samuel 23:29 Ittai), uncertain; Ribai, “Yahweh contends”; Gibeah, “hill”; Pirathonite, of Pirathon (Judges 12:15).
Hurai (2 Samuel 23:30 Hiddai), uncertain; Gaash, “quaking”; Abiel, “God is father”; Arbathite, of Beth-arabah (2 Samuel 23:31 Abi-albon).
Azmaveth, see 8:36; Baharumite, of Bahurim; Eliahba, “God hides”; Shaalbonite, of Shaalbim (“foxes”).
Second Samuel 23:32 reads “the sons of Jashen.” Hashem, “name”; Gizonite, uncertain; Shagee (2 Samuel 23:33 Shammah), uncertain; Hararite, perhaps “mountaineer.”
Ahiam, “mother’s brother”; Sachar (2 Samuel 23:33 Sharar), “reward”; Eliphal (2 Samuel 23:34 Eliphelet), “God judges”; Ur, “flame.”
Hepher, see 4:6; Mecherathite, uncertain; Ahijah, see 2:25. Second Samuel 23:34 reads here “Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite.”
Hezro, “enclosure”; Naarai (2 Samuel 23:35 Paarai the Arbite), “youthful”; Ezbai, uncertain.
Joel (2 Samuel 23:36 Igal), see 4:35; Nathan, see 2:36; Mibhar, “choice”; Hagri, “wanderer” (2 Samuel 23:36 “Bani the Gadite”).
Zelek, “cleft”; Ammonite, of Ammon (“people”); Naharai, “snorer”; Berothite, of Beeroth (“wells”).
Ira, see verse 28; Ithrite, of Jether’s clan (2:53); Gareb, “scabby.”
Second Samuel 23:39 ends the list with Uriah, adding “thirty-seven in all.” Uriah, “Yahweh is my light”; Hittite, see 1:13; Zabad, see 2:36; Ahlai, see 2:31.
Verses 42–47 are not in 2 Samuel. Adina, “delicate”; Shiza, uncertain. “And thirty with him” may mean “and over him were thirty.”
Hanan, see 8:23; Maacah, see 2:48; Joshaphat, “Yahweh has judged”; Mithnite, uncertain.
Uzzia, “Yahweh is my strength”; Ashterathite, of Ashtaroth (6:71); Shama, “he heard”; Jeiel, see 5:7 (Hebrew written text Jeuel); Hotham, see 7:32; Aroerite, of Aroer (5:8).
Jediael, see 7:6; Shimri, see 4:37; Joha, see 8:16; Tizite, uncertain.
Eliel, see 5:24; Mahavite, uncertain; Jeribai, “Yahweh contends”; Joshaviah, “Yahweh lets dwell”; Elnaam, “God is pleasantness”; Ithmah, “bereavement”; Moabite, of Moab (8:8).
Obed, see 2:12; Jaasiel, “God makes”; Mezobaite, perhaps of Zobah.

verses.text: Now these are they who came to David to Ziklag, while he yet kept himself close because of Saul the son of Kish.{a} They were among the mighty men, his helpers in war.
They were armed with bows and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and shooting arrows from the bow; they were of Saul’s kinsmen, of Benjamin.{b}
The chief was Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; and Jeziel and Pelet the sons of Azmaveth; and Beracah, and Jehu the Anathothite;{c}
and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and over the thirty; and Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite;{d}
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite;{e}
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;{f}
and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.{g}

From the Gadites some separated themselves to David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men of war fit for battle, who could handle shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions, and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains:{h}
Ezer the chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third,{i}
Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,{j}
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,{k}
Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,{l}
Jeremiah tenth, Machbannai eleventh.{m}
These of the sons of Gad were captains of the army; the least was equal to a hundred, and the greatest to a thousand.{n}

These are they who went over the Jordan in the first month (in March–April), when it had overflowed all its banks;{o} and they chased away all of the valleys, both toward the east and toward the west.
Some of the sons of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.

David went out to meet them and answered and said to them, “If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be joined to you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, although there is no violence in my hands, may the God of our fathers see it and judge.”

Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the thirty,{p} and he said, “Yours are we, David, and on your side, you son of Jesse! Peace, peace be to you, and peace be to those who help you; for your God is your helper.” So David took them in and made them captains of the band.

Some from Manasseh also deserted to David when he came with the Philistines to battle against Saul. Yet he did not help them, for the lords of the Philistines took counsel and sent him away, saying, “At the cost of our heads he will desert to his master Saul.”{q}
As he went to Ziklag, there deserted to him from Manasseh Adnah, and Jozabad, and Jediael, and Michael, and Jozabad, and Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands who belonged to Manasseh.{r}
They helped David against the band of raiders,{s} for they were all mighty men of valor, and they were captains in the army.
For from day to day men kept coming to David to help him, until there was a great army, like the army of God.{t}
These are the numbers of the heads of those armed for war who came to David at Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him, according to the word of Yahweh:{u}
The sons of Judah who bore shield and spear were six thousand eight hundred, armed for war.
Of the sons of Simeon, mighty men of valor for war, seven thousand one hundred.
Of the sons of Levi, four thousand six hundred.
Jehoiada was the leader of the house of Aaron, and with him were three thousand seven hundred;{v}
and Zadok, a young man, a mighty man of valor, and twenty-two captains of his father’s house.{w}
Of the sons of Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul, three thousand, for until then the greater part of them had kept their allegiance to the house of Saul.
Of the sons of Ephraim, twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers’ houses.
Of the half-tribe of Manasseh, eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and make David king.
Of the sons of Issachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, two hundred chiefs, and all their kinsmen under their command.{x}
Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the host, who could set the battle in array with all manner of instruments of war, fifty thousand, to help David{y} with an undivided heart.
Of Naphtali, a thousand captains, and with them, with shield and spear, thirty-seven thousand.
Of the Danites, twenty-eight thousand six hundred ready for battle.
Of Asher, forty thousand who could go out in the army, ready for battle.
From beyond the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, one hundred and twenty thousand with all kinds of weapons of war.{z}

All these were men of war who could order the battle line; they came with a perfect heart to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest of Israel too were of one heart to make David king.
They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had made provision for them.

Moreover those who were near to them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, on camels, on mules, and on oxen: provisions of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, oxen, and sheep in abundance; for there was joy in Israel.

notes.text: Ziklag, perhaps “winding”; Kish, see 8:30. See 1 Samuel 27:6. This chapter has no parallel in Samuel.
Benjamin, “son of the right hand,” makes the skill with the left hand notable (compare Judges 20:16).

So the Hebrew margin (Qere); the written text (Ketiv) reads Jezuel. Ahiezer, “my brother is help”; Joash, “Yahweh has given”; Shemaah, “report”; Gibeathite, of Gibeah (“hill”); Jeziel, perhaps “God sprinkles”; Pelet, see 2:47; Beracah, “blessing”; Jehu, “Yahweh is he”; Anathothite, see 11:28.

English verse 4 is Hebrew verses 4–5, so the Hebrew numbering of this chapter is one higher from here to the end (English 12:40 = Hebrew 12:41). Ishmaiah, “Yahweh hears”; Gibeonite, of Gibeon (“hill”); Jeremiah, “Yahweh exalts”; Jahaziel, “God sees”; Johanan, see 3:15; Jozabad, “Yahweh has given”; Gederathite, of Gederah (“sheepfold,” 4:23).
So the Hebrew margin (Qere); the written text (Ketiv) reads Hariphite. Eluzai, “God is my strength”; Jerimoth, see 7:7; Bealiah, “Yahweh is lord”; Shemariah, “Yahweh guards”; Shephatiah, see 3:3.

Elkanah, see 6:23; Isshiah, “Yahweh lends”; Azarel, “God helps”; Joezer, “Yahweh is help”; Jashobeam, see 11:11; Korahites, descendants of Korah (2:43), possibly a Benjaminite family of that name rather than the Levites.
Joelah, perhaps “may he avail”; Zebadiah, “Yahweh has given”; Jeroham, see 6:27; Gedor, “wall” (4:4).
Gadites, of Gad (“fortune”).
Ezer, “help”; Obadiah, “servant of Yahweh”; Eliab, see 2:13.
Mishmannah, “fatness”; Jeremiah, see verse 4.
Attai, see 2:35; Eliel, see 5:24.
Johanan, see 3:15; Elzabad, “God has given.”
Machbannai, perhaps “clad with a mantle.”
Or “one was over a hundred, and the greatest over a thousand.”
Hebrew “the first month” (Nisan, from the spring new year), the season of the barley harvest, when the Jordan floods (Joshua 3:15). “Banks”: so the Hebrew margin (Qere).
So the written Hebrew text (Ketiv); the Hebrew margin (Qere) reads “the officers.” Amasai, “burden-bearer” (6:25); some identify him with Amasa (2 Samuel 17:25).
See 1 Samuel 29:1–11. Manasseh, “causing to forget.”
Adnah, “pleasure”; Jozabad, see verse 4; Jediael, see 7:6; Michael, see 5:13; Elihu, “he is my God”; Zillethai, “shade.”
Probably the Amalekite raiders of 1 Samuel 30.
Or “a very great army.”
Verses 23–37 are a tribal muster list found only in Chronicles; some take the Hebrew ’eleph here as “unit” rather than “thousand.”
Jehoiada, see 11:22; Aaron, see 6:3.
Zadok, see 6:8.
Issachar, perhaps “there is reward.”
So the Septuagint; Hebrew lacks “David.” Zebulun, “dwelling.”
Reubenites, of Reuben (“see, a son”).

verses.text: David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

And David said to all the assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if it is from Yahweh our God, let us send abroad everywhere to our brothers who remain in all the land of Israel, and with them to the priests and Levites in their cities that have pasture lands, that they may gather themselves to us.
And let us bring again the ark of our God to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul.”{a}
All the assembly said that they would do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
So David assembled all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.{b}

And David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, Yahweh, who sits enthroned above the cherubim, where his name is called.{c}
They carried the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.{d}
David and all Israel played before God with all their might, even with songs, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.
When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark, for the oxen stumbled.{e}
The anger of Yahweh burned against Uzza, and he struck him because he put his hand to the ark; and there he died before God.
David was angry because Yahweh had broken out against Uzza; and that place is called Perez-uzza to this day.{f}
David was afraid of God that day, saying, “How can I bring the ark of God home to me?”
So David did not take the ark home to himself in the city of David, but turned it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.{g}
The ark of God remained with the household of Obed-edom in his house three months. And Yahweh blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that he had.

notes.text: Verses 5–14 parallel 2 Samuel 6:1–11. Verses 1–4 are found only in Chronicles.
Shihor, “black” or “turbid,” probably a branch of the Nile or the Wadi of Egypt; Hamath, “fortress.” Lebo-hamath may be a place name. Kiriath-jearim, “city of forests.”
Baalah, “mistress.” Second Samuel 6:2 reads “Baale-judah.” Cherubim, winged guardian figures.
Abinadab, see 2:13 (a different man); Uzza, “strength”; Ahio, “his brother” (the Septuagint takes it as “his brothers”).
Second Samuel 6:6 reads “Nacon.” Chidon may mean “javelin.”
Perez-uzza means “outburst against Uzza.”
Obed-edom, “servant of Edom”; Gittite, of Gath (“winepress”).

verses.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.{a}
And David knew that Yahweh had established him as king over Israel, for his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of his people Israel.
David took more wives at Jerusalem, and David became the father of more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children whom he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,{b}
Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,{c}
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.{d}
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went out against them.
Now the Philistines had come and made a raid in the Valley of Rephaim.
David inquired of God, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” Yahweh said to him, “Go up, for I will give them into your hand.”

So they came up to Baal-perazim, and David struck them down there. And David said, “God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like a breaking through of waters.” Therefore they called the name of that place Baal-perazim.{e}
They left their gods there, and David gave command, and they were burned with fire.{f}
Yet again the Philistines made a raid in the valley.
And when David inquired again of God, God said to him, “You shall not go up after them. Turn away from them and come against them opposite the balsam trees.{g}
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the army of the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer.{h}
And the fame of David went out into all lands, and Yahweh brought the fear of him upon all nations.

notes.text: Verses 1–16 parallel 2 Samuel 5:11–25. Hiram, perhaps “my brother is exalted”; Tyre, “rock.” The Hebrew margin (Qere) reads Hiram; the written text (Ketiv) reads Huram.
Compare the list at 3:5–8. Shammua (3:5 Shimea), “heard”; Shobab, see 2:18; Nathan, see 2:36; Solomon, see 3:5.
Elpelet corresponds to Eliphelet in 3:6. Ibhar, see 3:6; Elishua, “God is salvation.”
Beeliada, “the Lord knows” (3:8 Eliada, “God knows,” perhaps a later change avoiding the name Baal). Second Samuel 5:14–16 omits Nogah and Elpelet.
Baal-perazim means “lord of breakings through.”
Second Samuel 5:21 says that David and his men carried the idols away. Chronicles says they were burned, as Deuteronomy 7:5, 25 commands.
Or “baca trees”; the exact kind of tree is uncertain.
Second Samuel 5:25 reads “from Geba.” Gezer, “portion.”

verses.text: David made houses for himself in the city of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
Then David said, “No one may carry the ark of God except the Levites, for Yahweh chose them to carry the ark of Yahweh and to minister to him forever.”{a}
And David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of Yahweh to its place, which he had prepared for it.
David gathered together the sons of Aaron and the Levites:
of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brothers, a hundred and twenty;{b}
of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brothers, two hundred and twenty;{c}
of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brothers, a hundred and thirty;{d}
of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brothers, two hundred;{e}
of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brothers, eighty;{f}
of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brothers, a hundred and twelve.{g}
David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab,{h}

and said to them, “You are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites. Sanctify yourselves, both you and your brothers, that you may bring up the ark of Yahweh, the God of Israel, to the place that I have prepared for it.
For because you did not bear it at the first, Yahweh our God made a breach upon us, for we did not seek him after the ordinance.”
So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of Yahweh, the God of Israel.
The sons of the Levites bore the ark of God upon their shoulders with its poles, just as Moses commanded by the word of Yahweh.{i}
David also told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their brothers as the singers, with instruments of music, harps and lyres and cymbals, sounding aloud, to lift up the voice with joy.
So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel; and of his brothers, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their brothers, Ethan the son of Kushaiah;{j}

and with them their brothers of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben,{k} Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and Obed-edom and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.{l}
The singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were to sound aloud with cymbals of bronze;
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah, with harps set to Alamoth;{m}
and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah, with lyres set to the Sheminith, to lead.{n}
Chenaniah, chief of the Levites in carrying, was in charge of the carrying; he gave instruction about it, because he was skillful.{o}
Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark.{p}
Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, were to blow the trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.{q}
So David and the elders of Israel and the captains of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh from the house of Obed-edom with joy.{r}
And because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of Yahweh, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.{s}
David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who carried the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the leader of the carrying of the singers;{t} and David wore a linen ephod.
So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh with shouting, with the sound of the horn, with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with harps and lyres.
As the ark of the covenant of Yahweh came to the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.{u}

notes.text: See Numbers 4:15; Deuteronomy 10:8. Levites, of Levi (“joined”).
Kohath, see 6:1; Uriel, see 6:24.
Merari, see 6:1; Asaiah, see 4:36.
Gershom (Gershon), see 6:1; Joel, see 4:35.
Elizaphan, “God has hidden,” a Kohathite (Numbers 3:30); Shemaiah, see 3:22.
Hebron, see 6:2; Eliel, see 5:24.
Uzziel, see 6:2; Amminadab, see 6:22.
Zadok, see 6:8; Abiathar, “the father is abundant.”
See Exodus 25:14; Numbers 7:9. Moses, see 6:3.
Heman, see 6:33; Asaph, see 6:39; Berechiah, see 3:20; Ethan, see 6:42; Kushaiah (6:44 Kishi), perhaps “bow of Yahweh.”
Ben (“son”) is probably a copying error; it is lacking in the Septuagint and in verse 20.

Zechariah, see 5:7; Jaaziel (verse 20 Aziel), “God strengthens”; Shemiramoth, perhaps “name of heights”; Jehiel, “God lives”; Unni, perhaps “afflicted”; Eliab, see 2:13; Benaiah, see 4:36; Maaseiah, “work of Yahweh”; Mattithiah, “gift of Yahweh”; Eliphelehu, “God distinguishes him”; Mikneiah, “possession of Yahweh”; Obed-edom, see 13:13; Jeiel, see 5:7.
Alamoth, “young women,” probably a musical term for a higher register (compare Psalm 46 heading).
Sheminith, “the eighth,” probably a musical term for a lower register or an eight-stringed instrument (compare Psalms 6, 12 headings). Azaziah, “Yahweh is strong.”
Or “in charge of the music … he instructed in music”; the Hebrew massa’ can mean “carrying” or “lifting up the voice.” Chenaniah, “Yahweh establishes.”
Elkanah, see 6:23.
Shebaniah, “Yahweh has brought back”; Joshaphat, see 11:43; Nethanel, see 2:14; Amasai, see 6:25; Eliezer, “God is help”; Jehiah, “Yahweh lives.”
Verses 25–29 parallel 2 Samuel 6:12–16.
Second Samuel 6:13 says that when the bearers had gone six paces he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
Second Samuel 6:14 says only that David danced with all his might, wearing a linen ephod. “Of the singers” is perhaps a copying addition. An ephod was a linen garment worn by priests.
Michal, “who is like God?”

verses.text: They brought in the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.{a}
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh,
and he distributed to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat,{b} and a cake of raisins.
He appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of Yahweh, to commemorate, to thank, and to praise Yahweh, the God of Israel:
Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with harps and with lyres; and Asaph was to sound the cymbals;{c}
and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.{d}
Then on that day David for the first time committed to Asaph and his brothers the giving of thanks to Yahweh:
Give thanks to Yahweh; call on his name. Make his deeds known among the peoples.{e}
Sing to him; sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works.
Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice.
Seek Yahweh and his strength. Seek his face continually.
Remember his wonderful works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
you offspring of Israel his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.{f}
He is Yahweh our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever,{g} the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob for a statute, to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the portion of your inheritance,”
when you were but few in number,{h} very few, and sojourners in it.
They went about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no man to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes:
“Do not touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”
Sing to Yahweh, all the earth!{i} Proclaim his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised. He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols,{j} but Yahweh made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and joy are in his place.{k}
Ascribe to Yahweh, you families of the peoples, ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength.
Ascribe to Yahweh the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come before him. Worship Yahweh in holy array.{l}
Tremble before him, all the earth. The world also is established, so that it cannot be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice! Let them say among the nations, “Yahweh reigns!”
Let the sea roar, and its fullness! Let the field rejoice, and all that is therein!
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.
O give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good;{m} for his steadfast love endures forever.
Say, “Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us together and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name, and glory in your praise.”
Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting. And all the people said, “Amen,” and praised Yahweh.{n}
So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of Yahweh to minister before the ark continually, as each day’s work required,
and Obed-edom with his brothers, sixty-eight; and Obed-edom the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be gatekeepers.{o}
And he left Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests before the tabernacle of Yahweh in the high place that was at Gibeon,{p}
to offer burnt offerings to Yahweh on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, according to all that is written in the Law of Yahweh, which he commanded Israel.
With them were Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest who were chosen, who were mentioned by name, to give thanks to Yahweh, because his steadfast love endures forever.{q}
Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for those who should sound aloud, and instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were to be at the gate.
And all the people departed, each to his house, and David returned to bless his household.{r}

notes.text: Verses 1–3 parallel 2 Samuel 6:17–19.
The meaning of the Hebrew ’eshpar is uncertain; others suggest “a date cake.”
Jeiel (second): some read Jaaziel or Aziel, as in 15:18, 20.
Jahaziel, see 12:4.
Verses 8–22 parallel Psalm 105:1–15.
Psalm 105:6 reads “offspring of Abraham.”
Psalm 105:8 reads “He has remembered his covenant forever.”
Psalm 105:12 reads “when they were.”
Verses 23–33 parallel Psalm 96:1–13, with differences.
Hebrew ’elilim, “worthless things,” a play on ’elohim, “gods.”
Psalm 96:6 reads “Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.”
Or “in the splendor of holiness.”
Verses 34–36 parallel Psalm 106:1, 47–48. Psalm 106:47 reads “Save us, Yahweh our God.”
Psalm 106:48 ends “Let all the people say, ‘Amen!’ Praise Yah!”
Jeduthun, “praising”; Hosah, “refuge.” Obed-edom, see 13:13.
Gibeon, “hill”; compare 21:29; 2 Chronicles 1:3.
See 2 Chronicles 5:13; 7:3; Psalms 106:1; 136:1.
Second Samuel 6:19–20 parallels this verse; Chronicles omits Michal’s rebuke of David (2 Samuel 6:20–23).

verses.text: When David was living in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of Yahweh is under curtains.”{a}
Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you.”
But that same night the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
“Go and tell David my servant, ‘Thus says Yahweh: You shall not build me a house to dwell in.{b}
For I have not lived in a house since the day that I brought up Israel to this day, but have gone from tent to tent and from tabernacle to tabernacle.{c}

In all places where I have walked with all Israel, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”’{d}
Now therefore you shall say to my servant David, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people Israel.
I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. And I will make you a name, like the name of the great ones who are in the earth.

I will appoint a place for my people Israel and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. The children of wickedness shall not waste them any more, as at the first,
and from the days that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. And I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover I tell you that Yahweh will build you a house.{e}
When your days are fulfilled for you to go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who shall be of your sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
He shall build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be his father, and he shall be my son.{f} I will not take my steadfast love away from him, as I took it from him who was before you.
But I will settle him in my house and in my kingdom forever, and his throne shall be established forever.’”{g}
According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
Then King David went in and sat before Yahweh and said, “Who am I, Yahweh God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?

And this was a small thing in your eyes, O God. You have also spoken of your servant’s house for a great while to come, and have regarded me according to the standard of a man of high degree,{h} Yahweh God.
What more can David say to you about the honor done to your servant? For you know your servant.
Yahweh, for your servant’s sake, and according to your own heart, you have worked all this greatness, to make known all these great things.{i}
Yahweh, there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

What one nation in the earth is like your people Israel, whom God went to redeem to be his own people, to make for yourself a name by great and awesome things, in driving out nations from before your people whom you redeemed out of Egypt?{j}
For you made your people Israel your own people forever; and you, Yahweh, became their God.
Now, Yahweh, let the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house be established forever, and do as you have spoken.
Let your name be established and magnified forever, saying, ‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, is Israel’s God’; and the house of David your servant shall be established before you.
For you, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build him a house. Therefore your servant has found courage to pray before you.
Now, Yahweh, you are God, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
Now it has pleased you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you. For you, Yahweh, have blessed, and it is blessed forever.”{k}

notes.text: Verses 1–27 parallel 2 Samuel 7:1–29. Chronicles omits “Yahweh had given him rest from all his enemies around him” (2 Samuel 7:1). Nathan, “he has given.”
Second Samuel 7:5 has a question: “Shall you build me a house to dwell in?”
Hebrew “from tent to tent and from tabernacle”; the words “to tabernacle” are supplied from the sense. Compare 2 Samuel 7:6.
Hebrew shophet, “judge”; 2 Samuel 7:7 reads shibte, “tribes,” probably a copying difference.
Second Samuel 7:11 reads “Yahweh will make you a house”; the house here is a dynasty.
Chronicles omits 2 Samuel 7:14b, “When he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men.”
Second Samuel 7:16 reads “your house and your kingdom … before you … your throne.” Chronicles speaks of God’s house and kingdom.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain; compare 2 Samuel 7:19, “and this is the law for man.”
Second Samuel 7:21 reads “For your word’s sake.”
Second Samuel 7:23 adds “from Egypt, the nations and their gods.”
Some witnesses read “and may it be blessed forever.”

verses.text: After this David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines.{a}
He struck Moab, and the Moabites became servants to David and brought tribute.{b}
David also struck Hadarezer king of Zobah, toward Hamath, as he went to establish his dominion at the river Euphrates.{c}
David took from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen. And David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left enough of them for a hundred chariots.{d}
When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadarezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians.{e}
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to David and brought tribute. Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.
David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadarezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
From Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadarezer, David took very much bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the vessels of bronze.{f}
When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the host of Hadarezer king of Zobah,{g}

he sent Hadoram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadarezer and struck him; for Hadarezer had been at war with Tou. And he sent all kinds of vessels of gold and silver and bronze.{h}

These also King David dedicated to Yahweh, with the silver and the gold which he carried away from all the nations, from Edom, and from Moab, and from the sons of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
Moreover Abishai son of Zeruiah slew of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt eighteen thousand.{i}
He put garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became servants to David. And Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.
So David reigned over all Israel, and he executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;{j}
and Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar were priests; and Shavsha was secretary;{k}
and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief officials in the service of the king.{l}

notes.text: Verses 1–17 parallel 2 Samuel 8:1–18. Second Samuel 8:1 reads “took Metheg-ammah,” perhaps “the bridle of the mother city.” Gath, “winepress.”
Chronicles omits the execution of two-thirds of the Moabite captives (2 Samuel 8:2).
Hadarezer, “Hadad is help” (2 Samuel 8:3 Hadadezer); Zobah, an Aramean kingdom; Euphrates, see 5:9.
Second Samuel 8:4 reads “a thousand seven hundred horsemen” and does not mention the chariots; the Septuagint of Samuel agrees with Chronicles.
Syrians, Hebrew “Aram”; Damascus, perhaps “well-watered.”
Second Samuel 8:8 reads “Betah and Berothai” and does not mention Solomon’s use of the bronze. Tibhath, “slaughter”; Cun, perhaps “established.” On the bronze sea, see 2 Chronicles 4:2–5.
Tou (2 Samuel 8:9 Toi), uncertain.
Hadoram, “Hadad is exalted” (2 Samuel 8:10 Joram, “Yahweh is exalted”).

Second Samuel 8:13 credits David himself (“when he returned from striking eighteen thousand Arameans,” perhaps a misreading of Edom); Psalm 60 heading credits Joab with twelve thousand. Edomites, of Edom (“red”).
Jehoshaphat, “Yahweh has judged”; Ahilud, “a brother is born.”

Second Samuel 8:17 reads “Ahimelech the son of Abiathar” (as do many Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and the Vulgate here) and “Seraiah,” who is called Sheva in 2 Samuel 20:25 and Shisha in 1 Kings 4:3. Ahitub, see 6:7; Abimelech, “my father is king”; Shavsha, uncertain.
Second Samuel 8:18 reads “and David’s sons were priests.” Cherethites and Pelethites, the king’s foreign guard, perhaps Cretans and Philistines.

verses.text: After this Nahash the king of the sons of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place.{a}

David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the sons of Ammon to Hanun to comfort him.{b}

But the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun, “Do you think David honors your father, because he has sent comforters to you? Have not his servants come to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out the land?”
So Hanun took David’s servants and shaved them and cut off their garments in the middle, as far as their hips, and sent them away.
Some people went and told David about the men, and he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. The king said, “Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”{c}

When the sons of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the sons of Ammon sent about 37 tons of silver{d} to hire chariots and horsemen for themselves from Mesopotamia, from Aram-maacah, and from Zobah.{e}

So they hired thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah with his people, who came and encamped before Medeba. The sons of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities and came to battle.{f}
When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of the mighty men.
The sons of Ammon came out and set the battle in array at the gate of the city, and the kings who had come were by themselves in the field.
Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose out of all the choice men of Israel and set them in array against the Syrians.
The rest of the people he put in the hand of Abishai his brother, and they set themselves in array against the sons of Ammon.
He said, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will help you.
Be of good courage, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. And may Yahweh do what seems good to him.”
So Joab and the people who were with him drew near before the Syrians to the battle, and they fled before him.
When the sons of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother and entered the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

When the Syrians saw that they had been put to the worse before Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the River, with Shophach the captain of the host of Hadarezer at their head.{g}

It was told David, and he gathered all Israel together and crossed over the Jordan, and came upon them and set the battle in array against them. So when David had set the battle in array against the Syrians, they fought with him.
The Syrians fled before Israel, and David killed of the Syrians the men of seven thousand chariots and forty thousand footmen, and put to death Shophach the captain of the host.{h}
When the servants of Hadarezer saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they made peace with David and served him. So the Syrians would not help the sons of Ammon any more.

notes.text: Verses 1–19 parallel 2 Samuel 10:1–19. Nahash, “serpent”; Ammon, “people.”
Hanun, “favored.”
Jericho, perhaps “moon city.”
Hebrew “a thousand talents”; about 34 metric tons. Not mentioned in 2 Samuel 10:6.
Hebrew Aram-naharaim, “Aram of the two rivers.” Second Samuel 10:6 names Beth-rehob, Zobah, Maacah, and Tob. Maacah, see 2:48.

Second Samuel 10:6 reads “twenty thousand foot soldiers … and twelve thousand men of Tob,” giving the same total of thirty-two thousand, but footmen rather than chariots. Medeba, perhaps “waters of quiet.”
Shophach (2 Samuel 10:16 Shobach), perhaps “pouring.” The River is the Euphrates.
Second Samuel 10:18 reads “the men of seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen.”

verses.text: At the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out to battle, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the sons of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem. And Joab struck Rabbah and overthrew it.{a}

David took the crown of their king from off his head,{b} and found it to weigh about 75 pounds of gold,{c} and there were precious stones in it; and it was set on David’s head. He brought out the spoil of the city in great abundance.

He brought out the people who were in it and set them to work with saws, with iron picks, and with axes.{d} David did so to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
It came to pass after this that there arose war with the Philistines at Gezer; at that time Sibbecai the Hushathite slew Sippai, of the sons of the giants;{e} and the Philistines were brought low.
There was again war with the Philistines, and Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.{f}
There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand and six on each foot; and he also was descended from the giants.{g}
When he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea, David’s brother, killed him.{h}
These were descended from the giants in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

notes.text: Verses 1–3 parallel 2 Samuel 11:1; 12:26, 30–31. Chronicles omits the story of Bathsheba and Uriah (2 Samuel 11:2–12:25) and Joab’s summons to David (2 Samuel 12:27–29). Rabbah, “great (city).”
Or “the crown of Milcom,” the god of the Ammonites; the Hebrew consonants malkam can be read either way.
Hebrew “a talent”; about 34 kilograms.
So 2 Samuel 12:31; Hebrew “and he sawed them with the saw, with iron picks, and with saws.” The verb wayyasar (“and he sawed”) may be a copying error for wayyasem (“and he set them”).
Hebrew “of the Rephaim.” Second Samuel 21:18 reads “Saph” and “at Gob.” Sippai, perhaps “threshold.”

Second Samuel 21:19 reads “Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, the Bethlehemite, killed Goliath the Gittite.” Chronicles names Lahmi (from the last part of “the Bethlehemite”) as Goliath’s brother, reconciling the text with 1 Samuel 17. Jair, “he enlightens”; Lahmi, perhaps “my bread”; Goliath, uncertain.
Verses 6–8 parallel 2 Samuel 21:20–22.
Jonathan, see 2:32; Shimea, see 2:13.

verses.text: Satan stood up against Israel and moved David to number Israel.{a}
David said to Joab and to the princes of the people, “Go, count Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring me word, that I may know their number.”{b}

Joab said, “May Yahweh make his people a hundred times as many as they are! But, my lord the king, are they not all my lord’s servants? Why then does my lord require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Israel?”
Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Joab. Therefore Joab departed and went throughout all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.

Joab gave the sum of the numbering of the people to David. All those of Israel were one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword; and in Judah were four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword.{c}
But he did not count Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king’s word was abhorrent to Joab.{d}
God was displeased with this thing, so he struck Israel.
David said to God, “I have sinned greatly in doing this thing. But now, please take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
Yahweh spoke to Gad, David’s seer, saying,{e}
“Go and speak to David, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh: I offer you three things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.’”
So Gad came to David and said to him, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Take your choice:

either three years of famine; or three months to be swept away before your foes, while the sword of your enemies overtakes you; or else three days of the sword of Yahweh, even pestilence in the land, and the angel of Yahweh destroying throughout all the borders of Israel.’ Now therefore consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me.”{f}
David said to Gad, “I am in great distress. Let me fall now into the hand of Yahweh, for very great are his mercies; and let me not fall into the hand of man.”
So Yahweh sent a pestilence on Israel, and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men.

And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. As he was about to destroy, Yahweh looked, and he relented of the evil, and said to the destroying angel, “It is enough; now stay your hand.” The angel of Yahweh was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.{g}

David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of Yahweh standing between earth and heaven, having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on their faces.{h}

David said to God, “Is it not I who commanded the people to be numbered? It is I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand, Yahweh my God, be against me and against my father’s house, but not against your people, that they should be plagued.”
Then the angel of Yahweh commanded Gad to say to David that David should go up and set up an altar to Yahweh on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David went up at the saying of Gad, which he had spoken in Yahweh’s name.
Ornan turned back and saw the angel, and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat.{i}
As David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and went out of the threshing floor and bowed himself to David with his face to the ground.

Then David said to Ornan, “Give me the site of this threshing floor, that I may build on it an altar to Yahweh. You shall sell it to me for the full price, that the plague may be stopped from the people.”

Ornan said to David, “Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good in his eyes. Look, I give the oxen for burnt offerings, and the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering; I give it all.”
King David said to Ornan, “No, but I will surely buy it for the full price. For I will not take what is yours for Yahweh, nor offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing.”
So David gave to Ornan for the place gold weighing about fifteen pounds.{j}
David built there an altar to Yahweh and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on Yahweh; and he answered him from heaven by fire on the altar of burnt offering.{k}
Then Yahweh commanded the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, when David saw that Yahweh had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
For the tabernacle of Yahweh, which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering, were at that time in the high place at Gibeon.
But David could not go before it to inquire of God, for he was afraid because of the sword of the angel of Yahweh.

notes.text: Verses 1–27 parallel 2 Samuel 24:1–25. Second Samuel 24:1 says “The anger of Yahweh was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them.” Hebrew satan, without the article, may be read as the proper name Satan or as “an adversary.”
Beersheba, “well of seven” or “well of the oath”; Dan, “judge.” Chronicles omits the route of the census (2 Samuel 24:5–8).

Second Samuel 24:9 reads “in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men … and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand.” The figures cannot be fully reconciled; Chronicles may include the standing army (27:1–15) or follow a different source.
This explanation is found only in Chronicles; compare Numbers 1:47–49.
Gad, “fortune.”
Second Samuel 24:13 reads “seven years of famine” (the Septuagint of Samuel reads “three years,” as here).
Ornan (2 Samuel 24:16 Araunah), perhaps a Hurrian name or title, “lord.”
This verse is not in the standard text of 2 Samuel, but a Dead Sea Scroll of Samuel (4QSam-a) has a similar verse at 2 Samuel 24:16.
Second Samuel 24:20 says only that Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him.

Hebrew “six hundred shekels of gold by weight,” about 6.9 kilograms. Second Samuel 24:24 says David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver, about 1¼ pounds (575 grams). Chronicles speaks of the whole “place,” the future temple site.
See Leviticus 9:24; 1 Kings 18:38. The fire from heaven is not mentioned in 2 Samuel.

verses.text: Then David said, “This is the house of Yahweh God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”{a}
David commanded to gather together the foreigners who were in the land of Israel, and he set stonecutters to cut dressed stones to build the house of God.
David prepared iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and bronze in abundance beyond weighing,
and cedar trees without number; for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought cedar trees in abundance to David.{b}

David said, “Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for Yahweh must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and of glory throughout all countries. I will therefore make preparation for it.” So David prepared abundantly before his death.
Then he called for Solomon his son and charged him to build a house for Yahweh, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, “My son, as for me, it was in my heart to build a house to the name of Yahweh my God.

But the word of Yahweh came to me, saying, ‘You have shed blood abundantly and have made great wars. You shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood upon the earth in my sight.

Behold, a son shall be born to you, who shall be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his enemies all around; for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days.{c}
He shall build a house for my name. He shall be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’
Now, my son, may Yahweh be with you, so that you may prosper and build the house of Yahweh your God, as he has spoken concerning you.
Only may Yahweh give you discretion and understanding, and give you charge over Israel, that you may keep the law of Yahweh your God.
Then you will prosper, if you are careful to do the statutes and the ordinances which Yahweh commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid, nor be dismayed.

Now see, in my affliction I have prepared for the house of Yahweh about 3,750 tons of gold and 37,500 tons of silver,{d} and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for it is in abundance. I have also prepared timber and stone, and you may add to them.
There are also workmen with you in abundance, cutters and workers of stone and timber, and all kinds of men who are skillful in every kind of work.
Of the gold, the silver, the bronze, and the iron, there is no number. Arise and be doing, and may Yahweh be with you.”
David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,

“Is not Yahweh your God with you? And has he not given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before Yahweh and before his people.

Now set your heart and your soul to seek Yahweh your God. Arise therefore and build the sanctuary of Yahweh God, to bring the ark of the covenant of Yahweh and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for the name of Yahweh.”

notes.text: This verse identifies Ornan’s threshing floor as the site of the temple; compare 2 Chronicles 3:1.
Sidonians, of Sidon (“fishing”); Tyrians, of Tyre (14:1).
Solomon (Hebrew Shelomoh) sounds like shalom, “peace.”

Hebrew “a hundred thousand talents of gold and a million talents of silver”: about 3,750 tons (3,400 metric tons) of gold and 37,500 tons (34,000 metric tons) of silver. The figures are enormous, perhaps intentionally hyperbolic; compare 29:4, 7.

verses.text: When David was old and full of days, he made Solomon his son king over Israel.{a}
And he assembled all the princes of Israel, and the priests and the Levites.
The Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward, and their number, counted head by head, was thirty-eight thousand men.{b}
“Of these,” David said, “twenty-four thousand shall oversee the work of the house of Yahweh, six thousand shall be officers and judges,
four thousand shall be gatekeepers, and four thousand shall praise Yahweh with the instruments that I made for praise.”{c}
David divided them into divisions corresponding to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.{d}
The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, and Zetham, and Joel, three.{e}
The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ houses of Ladan.{f}
And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.{g}
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; Jeush and Beriah, however, had few sons, and therefore they were reckoned as one father’s house, one assignment.{h}
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was separated, that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before Yahweh, to minister to him, and to bless in his name forever.
But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.{i}
The sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.{j}
The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.{k}
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.{l}
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.{m}
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died having no sons, only daughters; and their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.{n}

These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of those who were enrolled, by the number of names counted head by head, who did the work for the service of the house of Yahweh, from twenty years old and upward.{o}
For David said, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.
So the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of its vessels for its service.”
For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were numbered from twenty years old and upward.

Their office was to be at the side of the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of Yahweh, in the courts and in the chambers, in the cleansing of everything holy, and in any work for the service of the house of God;
also for the showbread, for the fine flour for a grain offering, for the unleavened wafers, for the baked offering, for the offering mixed with oil, and for all measures of quantity and size.
They were to stand every morning to thank and praise Yahweh, and likewise at evening,
and whenever burnt offerings were offered to Yahweh on the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the appointed feasts, in the number required of them, continually before Yahweh.
Thus they were to keep charge of the tent of meeting and charge of the holy place, and to attend the sons of Aaron their brothers for the service of the house of Yahweh.

notes.text: Compare 1 Kings 1:1–40, where Solomon is made king amid a struggle for succession; Chronicles does not narrate that struggle.

Numbers 4:3 sets the age at thirty; Numbers 8:24 at twenty-five. In verses 24 and 27 of this chapter the age is twenty, as in 2 Chronicles 31:17 and Ezra 3:8. Verse 27 explains the change as David’s last instruction.
Hebrew “that I made”; the Septuagint reads “that he made.”
Ladan (6:17 and Exodus 6:17 Libni), perhaps “for pleasure”; Shimei, see 4:26.
Jehiel, see 15:18; Zetham, “olive tree”; Joel, see 4:35.
Some think Shimei here should be Jehiel, as Shimei’s sons follow in verse 10. Shelomoth, “peaceful”; Haziel, “God sees”; Haran, perhaps “mountaineer.”
Jahath, see 4:2; Zina (verse 11 Zizah; the Septuagint reads Ziza here), uncertain; Jeush, see 1:35; Beriah, see 7:23.
Or “a single class for duty.”
Shebuel (24:20 Shubael), perhaps “return, O God.” Gershom, see 6:16.
Rehabiah, “Yahweh has enlarged”; Eliezer, see 15:24.
Shelomith (24:22 Shelomoth), “peaceful.”
Jeriah, “Yahweh sees”; Amariah, see 6:7; Jahaziel, see 12:4; Jekameam, “may the people rise.”
Micah, see 5:5; Isshiah, see 12:6.
Mahli, see 6:19; Eder, “flock”; Jeremoth, “heights.”
See note on verse 3.

verses.text: The divisions of the sons of Aaron were these. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.{a}
But Nadab and Abihu died before their father and had no children, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.{b}
David, with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their offices in their service.{c}

There were more chief men found of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar, and so they were divided: sixteen heads of fathers’ houses of the sons of Eleazar, and eight of the sons of Ithamar, according to their fathers’ houses.
They divided them by lot, the one sort with the other; for there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God both of the sons of Eleazar and of the sons of Ithamar.

Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, one of the Levites, recorded them in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the priests and of the Levites: one father’s house being drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn for Ithamar.{d}
The first lot came forth to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,{e}
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,{f}
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,{g}
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,{h}
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,{i}
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,{j}
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,{k}
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,{l}
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,{m}
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,{n}
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,{o}
the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.{p}
This was their order for their service when they came into the house of Yahweh according to the procedure established for them by Aaron their father, as Yahweh, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
And of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.{q}
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
The sons of Hebron:{r} Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel, Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.{s}
The brother of Micah, Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Jaaziah: Beno.{t}
The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.{u}
Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
Of Kish, the sons of Kish: Jerahmeel.{v}
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites by their fathers’ houses.

These likewise cast lots even as their brothers the sons of Aaron, in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the priests and of the Levites, the head of each father’s house the same as his younger brother.

notes.text: Nadab, see 2:28; Abihu, “he is my father”; Eleazar, see 6:3; Ithamar, “island of palms.”
See Leviticus 10:1–2.
Ahimelech, “my brother is king.” Compare 18:16, where the Hebrew reads Abimelech.
Hebrew “one father’s house taken for Eleazar, and taken, taken for Ithamar”; the Septuagint reads “one to Eleazar, and one to Ithamar.” Shemaiah, see 3:22; Nethanel, see 2:14.
Jehoiarib (9:10 Jehoiarib), “Yahweh contends”; Jedaiah, see 4:37. The Maccabees were of the course of Jehoiarib (1 Maccabees 2:1).
Harim, “consecrated”; Seorim, “barley.”
Malchijah, “Yahweh is king”; Mijamin, “from the right hand.”
Hakkoz, “the thorn”; Abijah, “Yahweh is father.” Zechariah the father of John the Baptist belonged to the division of Abijah (Luke 1:5).
Jeshua, “Yahweh is salvation”; Shecaniah, “Yahweh has dwelt.”
Eliashib, see 3:24; Jakim, see 8:19.
Huppah, “canopy”; Jeshebeab, perhaps “father’s dwelling.”
Bilgah, “cheerfulness”; Immer, “lamb.”
Hezir, “swine”; Happizzez, “the shattering.”
Pethahiah, “Yahweh opens”; Jehezkel, “God strengthens” (the same name as Ezekiel).
Jachin, “he establishes”; Gamul, “weaned.”
Delaiah, see 3:24; Maaziah, “Yahweh is a refuge.”
Shubael, see 23:16; Jehdeiah, “Yahweh rejoices.”
“Of Hebron” and “the chief” are supplied from 23:19; the Hebrew reads “And my sons: Jeriah.”
So the Hebrew margin (Qere); the written text (Ketiv) reads Shamur. Shamir, “thorn.”
Jaaziah, “Yahweh strengthens”; Beno, “his son.” The Hebrew of verses 26–27 is uncertain; beno may mean “his son” rather than a name.
Shoham, “onyx”; Zaccur, see 4:26; Ibri, “Hebrew.”
Jerahmeel, see 2:9; Kish, see 23:21.

verses.text: David and the commanders of the army also set apart for service some of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with lyres, with harps, and with cymbals. The number of the workmen according to their service was:{a}
Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah, the sons of Asaph, under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied at the king’s order.{b}

Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei,{c} Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre in giving thanks and praising Yahweh.{d}
Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.{e}
All these were sons of Heman, the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up his horn;{f} and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

They were all under the direction of their father for song in the house of Yahweh with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman were under the direction of the king.
Their number, with their brothers who were trained in singing to Yahweh, all who were skilled, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
They cast lots for their duties, small and great alike, teacher as well as pupil.
The first lot fell for Asaph to Joseph;{g} the second to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and his sons, twelve;
the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve;{h}
the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;{i}
the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve;{j}
the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve;{k}
the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the fifteenth, to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;{l}
the sixteenth, to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the seventeenth, to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the eighteenth, to Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the nineteenth, to Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the twentieth, to Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the twenty-first, to Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the twenty-second, to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the twenty-third, to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the twenty-fourth, to Romamti-ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.{m}

notes.text: Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, see 6:33, 39; 16:41. Here their music is called prophecy (compare 2 Kings 3:15).
Zaccur, see 4:26; Joseph, “may he add”; Nethaniah, “Yahweh has given”; Asharelah (verse 14 Jesharelah), perhaps “upright toward God.”
Shimei is supplied from verse 17; the Hebrew and the Septuagint list five names but say “six.”
Gedaliah, “Yahweh is great”; Zeri (verse 11 Izri), perhaps “balm”; Jeshaiah, “Yahweh saves”; Hashabiah, see 6:45; Mattithiah, see 9:31.

Bukkiah, “flask of Yahweh”; Mattaniah, see 9:15; Uzziel, see 4:42; Shebuel (verse 20 Shubael), see 23:16; Jerimoth (verse 22 Jeremoth), see 7:7; Hananiah, “Yahweh is gracious”; Hanani, “gracious.” The remaining names, read together, form a short prayer: “Be gracious to me, Yah, be gracious to me; you are my God (Eliathah); I have magnified (Giddalti) and I have exalted (Romamti) help (ezer); sitting in hardship (Joshbekashah), I have spoken (Mallothi); he has given abundantly (Hothir) visions (Mahazioth).”
Hebrew “to lift up the horn,” an idiom for giving strength or honor.
The Hebrew gives no number for Joseph; the total of 288 (verse 7) implies twelve for each of the twenty-four lots.
Izri, see Zeri, verse 3.
Jesharelah, see verse 2 (Asharelah).
Azarel (verse 4 Uzziel), see 12:6.
Shubael, see verse 4 (Shebuel).
Jeremoth, see verse 4 (Jerimoth).
The twenty-four musical courses parallel the twenty-four priestly courses of chapter 24.

verses.text: As for the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.{a}
Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,{b}
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.{c}
Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,{d}
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.{e}
Also to Shemaiah his son were sons born who ruled over their fathers’ house, for they were mighty men of valor.
The sons of Shemaiah were Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, and Elzabad, whose brothers were strong men, Elihu, and Semachiah.{f}
All these were of the sons of Obed-edom; they and their sons and their brothers were able men with strength for the service, sixty-two of Obed-edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, able men, eighteen.
Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief),{g}
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.{h}
Of these were the divisions of the gatekeepers, by their chief men, having charges like their brothers, to minister in the house of Yahweh.
They cast lots, small and great alike, by their fathers’ houses, for each gate.
Eastward the lot fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counselor, they cast lots, and his lot came out northward.{i}
To Obed-edom southward, and to his sons the storehouse.{j}
To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway going up, guard beside guard.{k}
Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two.
For the Parbar westward, four at the causeway and two at the Parbar.{l}
These were the divisions of the doorkeepers, of the sons of the Korahites and of the sons of Merari.
Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of the house of God and over the treasures of the dedicated things.{m}
The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.{n}
The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of the house of Yahweh.
Of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasures.
His brothers: from Eliezer came Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.{o}

This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasures of the dedicated things which King David and the heads of the fathers’ houses, the officers of thousands and of hundreds, and the commanders of the army had dedicated.{p}
Out of the spoil taken in the wars they dedicated things to strengthen the house of Yahweh.
Also all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated, everything dedicated was in the care of Shelomoth and his brothers.{q}
Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to outside duties over Israel, as officers and judges.{r}
Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred able men, had oversight of Israel west of the Jordan, for all the work of Yahweh and for the service of the king.{s}

Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was chief of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ houses. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought out, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.{t}

King David appointed him and his brothers, two thousand seven hundred able men, heads of fathers’ houses, over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.

notes.text: Meshelemiah (verse 14 Shelemiah; 9:21), “Yahweh repays”; Kore, see 9:19. “Asaph” is perhaps a copying error for Ebiasaph (9:19).
Zechariah, see 9:21; Jediael, see 7:6; Zebadiah, see 8:15; Jathniel, “God gives.”
Elam, see 8:24; Jehohanan, “Yahweh is gracious”; Eliehoenai, “my eyes are toward Yahweh.”
Obed-edom, see 13:13; Shemaiah, see 3:22; Jehozabad, “Yahweh has given”; Joah, see 6:21; Sachar, see 11:35; Nethanel, see 2:14.
Ammiel, see 3:5; Issachar, see 12:32; Peullethai, “wage of Yahweh.” The blessing recalls 13:14.
Othni, perhaps “my strength”; Rephael, “God heals”; Obed, see 2:12; Elzabad, see 12:12; Elihu, see 12:20; Semachiah, “Yahweh sustains.”
Hosah, see 16:38; Shimri, see 4:37.
Hilkiah, see 6:13; Tebaliah, “Yahweh has immersed.”
Shelemiah, see verse 1.
Hebrew “the house of the gatherings,” a storehouse.
The Hebrew “Shuppim” may be a copying repetition of the last word of verse 15. Shallecheth, “casting out.”
Parbar, perhaps “colonnade” or “court”; the meaning is uncertain.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads “their brothers.” Ahijah, see 2:25.
Jehieli, a family name from Jehiel (23:8).
Joram, “Yahweh is exalted”; Zichri, see 8:19.
Shelomoth (Hebrew written text Shelomith), see 23:9.
Abner, “father of light”; Ner, see 8:33. Samuel, “name of God” or “heard by God.”
Chenaniah, see 15:22.
Hashabiah, see 6:45. Hebrew “beyond the Jordan westward,” as seen from the east; that is, west of the Jordan.
Jerijah (23:19 Jeriah), “Yahweh sees”; Jazer, “he helps.”

verses.text: This is the list of the people of Israel by their number, the heads of fathers’ houses, the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter concerning the divisions that came in and went out month after month throughout all the months of the year, each division being twenty-four thousand:{a}
Over the first division for the first month (in March–April) was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel; in his division were twenty-four thousand.{b}
He was of the children of Perez, the head of all the captains of the host for the first month.
Over the division of the second month (in April–May) was Dodai the Ahohite, with his division, and Mikloth was the leader; in his division were twenty-four thousand.{c}
