The third commander of the army, for the third month (in May–June), was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the priest, as chief; in his division were twenty-four thousand.{d}
This is the Benaiah who was a mighty man of the thirty and over the thirty; and over his division was Ammizabad his son.{e}
The fourth, for the fourth month (in June–July), was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; in his division were twenty-four thousand.{f}
The fifth commander, for the fifth month (in July–August), was Shamhuth the Izrahite; in his division were twenty-four thousand.{g}
The sixth, for the sixth month (in August–September), was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The seventh, for the seventh month (in September–October), was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month (in October–November), was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.{h}
The ninth, for the ninth month (in November–December), was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjaminites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month (in December–January), was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month (in January–February), was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the sons of Ephraim; in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month (in February–March), was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; in his division were twenty-four thousand.{i}
Furthermore, over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri was ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;{j}
of Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; of Aaron, Zadok;{k}
of Judah, Elihu, of the brothers of David; of Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;{l}
of Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jerimoth the son of Azriel;{m}
of the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;{n}
of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;{o}
of Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the princes of the tribes of Israel.{p}
But David did not count those from twenty years old and under, because Yahweh had said he would multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.
Joab the son of Zeruiah began to count them, but did not finish; and for this there came wrath on Israel; neither was the number put into the account of the chronicles of King David.{q}
Over the king’s treasuries was Azmaveth the son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the country, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah.{r}
Over those who did the work of the field, tilling the ground, was Ezri the son of Chelub.{s}
Over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; and over the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite.{t}
Over the olive trees and the sycamore-fig trees in the Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the stores of oil was Joash.{u}
Over the herds that grazed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite; and over the herds in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai.{v}
Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the female donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite.{w}
Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were stewards of King David’s property.{x}
Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding and a scribe; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni attended the king’s sons.{y}
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.{z}
After Ahithophel came Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar; and Joab was commander of the king’s army.{aa}

notes.text: The months in this chapter are numbered from the spring new year (Nisan); because the calendar was lunar, each month spans parts of two of ours.
Jashobeam, see 11:11; Zabdiel, “gift of God.” Perez, see 2:4.
Hebrew “Dodai the Ahohite and his division, and Mikloth the leader”; perhaps read “Eleazar the son of Dodai” (11:12). Dodai, “beloved”; Mikloth, see 8:32.
Or “the son of Jehoiada, the chief priest.” Benaiah, see 11:22.
Ammizabad, “my people has given.”
Asahel was killed by Abner before David reigned over all Israel (2 Samuel 2:23), so this list may reflect a time when his son Zebadiah held the post in his name.
Shamhuth, perhaps “desolation” (11:27 Shammoth the Harorite); Izrahite, perhaps a Zerahite of Judah.
Zerahites, of Zerah (2:4).
Heldai (11:30 Heled), “mole” or “enduring”; Othniel, “lion of God” or “God is my strength.”
Eliezer, see 15:24; Zichri, see 8:19; Shephatiah, see 3:3; Maacah, see 2:48. Gad and Asher are not listed; Levi and Aaron are counted separately.
Kemuel, “God raises up.”
The Septuagint reads Eliab, David’s eldest brother (2:13). Elihu, see 12:20; Omri, see 7:8; Michael, see 5:13.
Ishmaiah, see 12:4; Obadiah, see 12:9; Jerimoth, see 7:7; Azriel, see 5:24.
Hoshea, “salvation”; Azaziah, see 15:21; Pedaiah, see 3:18.
Iddo, see 6:21; Jaasiel, see 11:47; Abner, see 26:28.
Azarel, see 12:6; Jeroham, see 6:27.
See chapter 21. “Chronicles” here is Hebrew “the account of the days.”
Adiel, see 4:36; Uzziah, “Yahweh is strength.”
Ezri, “my help”; Chelub, see 4:11.
Ramathite, of Ramah (“height”); Zabdi, see 8:19; Shiphmite, perhaps of Shepham (Numbers 34:10).
Shephelah, “lowland,” the foothills west of Judah. Baal-hanan, “the Lord is gracious”; Gederite, of Geder; Joash, see 12:3.
Sharon, “plain”; Shitrai, perhaps “officer”; Shaphat, see 3:22; Adlai, uncertain.
Obil, “camel driver”; Ishmaelite, of Ishmael (“God hears”); Jehdeiah, see 24:20; Meronothite, of Meronoth.
Jaziz, perhaps “he moves”; Hagrite, see 5:10.
Or “nephew”; Hebrew dod, “uncle” or “beloved.” Jonathan, see 2:32; Jehiel, see 15:18; Hachmoni, “wise.”
Ahithophel, “brother of folly”; Hushai, “quick”; Archite, of the Archites (Joshua 16:2). See 2 Samuel 15:12, 32–37.
Jehoiada, see 11:22; Abiathar, see 15:11; Joab, see 2:16.

verses.text: David assembled at Jerusalem all the officials of Israel: the princes of the tribes, the captains of the divisions that served the king, the captains of thousands, the captains of hundreds, and the rulers over all the substance and possessions of the king and of his sons, together with the officers, the mighty men, and all the men of valor.

Then David the king stood up on his feet and said, “Hear me, my brothers and my people! As for me, it was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of Yahweh, and for the footstool of our God, and I had made ready to build it.{a}
But God said to me, ‘You will not build a house for my name, for you are a man of wars and have poured out blood.’

Yet Yahweh, the God of Israel, chose me out of all my father’s house to be king over Israel forever. For he chose Judah to be prince; and of the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father it pleased him to make me king over all Israel.
And of all my sons (for Yahweh has given me many sons) he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of Yahweh over Israel.{b}
He said to me, ‘Solomon your son, he shall build my house and my courts; for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is constant to do my commandments and my ordinances, as at this day.’

Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of Yahweh, and in the hearing of our God, keep and seek out all the commandments of Yahweh your God, that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children after you forever.

“You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind; for Yahweh searches all hearts and understands every purpose of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found of you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.
Take heed now, for Yahweh has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it.”
Then David gave Solomon his son the pattern of the porch of the temple, and of its houses, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner chambers, and the room for the mercy seat;{c}

and the pattern of all that he had in mind{d} for the courts of the house of Yahweh, for all the chambers around, for the treasuries of the house of God, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things;
also for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the work of the service of the house of Yahweh, and for all the vessels of service in the house of Yahweh;
of gold by weight for all the vessels of gold for every kind of service, and of silver by weight for all the vessels of silver for every kind of service;

the weight of gold for the lampstands and their lamps of gold, by the weight of each lampstand and its lamps; and for the lampstands of silver, silver by weight for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;
and gold by weight for the tables of showbread, for each table; and silver for the tables of silver;
and pure gold for the forks, the basins, and the cups; and for the golden bowls, gold by weight for each bowl; and for the silver bowls, silver by weight for each bowl;
and for the altar of incense, refined gold by weight; and gold for the pattern of the chariot, the cherubim that spread their wings and covered the ark of the covenant of Yahweh.{e}
“All this,” said David, “he made clear to me in writing from the hand of Yahweh, all the works of this pattern.”{f}

Then David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or dismayed, for Yahweh God, my God, is with you. He will not leave you nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of Yahweh is completed.

Behold, there are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; and there shall be with you in all kinds of work every willing, skillful man, for any manner of service; also the captains and all the people will be entirely at your command.”

notes.text: The ark as God’s footstool: compare Psalms 99:5; 132:7.
The kingdom is called “the kingdom of Yahweh”; compare 17:14; 29:23.
Hebrew “the house of the covering” (kapporet), the gold lid of the ark (Exodus 25:17–22).
Hebrew “that was with him by the spirit,” or “that he had by the Spirit.”
The cherubim are pictured as God’s chariot throne; compare Ezekiel 1; 10.
Or “All this he made clear to me in writing, because the hand of Yahweh was upon me.” The Hebrew is difficult.

verses.text: King David said to all the assembly, “Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great; for the palace is not for man but for Yahweh God.{a}

So I have provided for the house of my God with all my might: the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the bronze for the things of bronze, the iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; also onyx stones and stones for setting, stones of antimony and of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble in abundance.{b}
Moreover, because I delight in the house of my God, I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, and I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have provided for the holy house:
about 112 tons of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and about 262 tons of refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the houses,{c}

gold for the things of gold and silver for the things of silver, and for all manner of work to be made by the hands of artisans. Who then offers willingly to consecrate himself this day to Yahweh?”{d}
Then the heads of fathers’ houses, the princes of the tribes of Israel, the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and the officers over the king’s work offered willingly.
They gave for the service of the house of God about 188 tons of gold and about 185 pounds in gold coins,{e} about 375 tons of silver, about 675 tons of bronze, and about 3,750 tons of iron.{f}
Those with whom precious stones were found gave them to the treasure of the house of Yahweh, in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.{g}
Then the people rejoiced, for they offered willingly, because with a perfect heart they offered willingly to Yahweh. David the king also rejoiced with great joy.
Therefore David blessed Yahweh in the presence of all the assembly, and David said: “Blessed are you, Yahweh, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.{h}

Yours, Yahweh, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty; for all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, Yahweh, and you are exalted as head over all.{i}
Riches and honor come from before you, and you are ruler over all. In your hand is power and might; it is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to everyone.
Now therefore, our God, we thank you, and praise your glorious name.
“But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and of your own we have given you.
For we are strangers before you and sojourners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are like a shadow, and there is no abiding.{j}
Yahweh our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and is all your own.

I know also, my God, that you test the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have freely offered all these things; and now I have seen with joy your people who are present here offer willingly to you.
Yahweh, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever in the inclinations of the thoughts of the heart of your people, and direct their heart toward you.
Give to Solomon my son a whole heart to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do all of them, and to build the palace for which I have made provision.”
Then David said to all the assembly, “Now bless Yahweh your God.” And all the assembly blessed Yahweh, the God of their fathers, and bowed down and worshiped Yahweh and the king.{k}

On the next day they offered sacrifices to Yahweh and offered burnt offerings to Yahweh: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
They ate and drank before Yahweh on that day with great gladness. And they made Solomon the son of David king a second time, and anointed him to Yahweh to be prince, and Zadok to be priest.{l}
Then Solomon sat on the throne of Yahweh as king in place of David his father; and he prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the officials and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, pledged their allegiance to Solomon the king.{m}
Yahweh magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and bestowed on him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
Thus David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
The time that he reigned over Israel was forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.{n}
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
Now the acts of King David, first and last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the records of Gad the seer,{o}
with all his reign and his might, and the times that went over him, and over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the lands.

notes.text: Hebrew birah, “citadel” or “palace,” a late word used here of the temple.
The identity of several of these stones is uncertain. “Antimony” (Hebrew pukh) was used as eye paint; others take it as a dark or inlay stone.

Hebrew “three thousand talents of gold … seven thousand talents of refined silver”: about 102 metric tons of gold and 238 metric tons of silver. Ophir, a land famous for gold, perhaps in southern Arabia or east Africa.
Hebrew “to fill his hand,” an idiom for consecration.

Hebrew “ten thousand darics,” about 84 kilograms. The daric (Hebrew ’adarkon) was a Persian gold coin of about 8.4 grams, first minted under Darius I (about 515 B.C.). Its mention here is an anachronism: the writer gives the value in the currency of his own day. Some take the word as drachmas.

Hebrew “five thousand talents … ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron”: about 170 metric tons of gold, 340 metric tons of silver, 612 metric tons of bronze, and 3,400 metric tons of iron.
Jehiel, see 23:8.
Verses 10–13 are often called David’s prayer. The doxology added to the Lord’s Prayer in some late manuscripts of Matthew 6:13 echoes verse 11.
Or “and you are exalted over all as head.”
Or “and there is no hope.”
Bowing before the king is an act of honor, not of worship as given to God; the same Hebrew verb is used for both.
“A second time” refers back to 23:1. Compare 1 Kings 1:32–40, where Solomon is anointed by Zadok and Nathan.
Hebrew “gave a hand under Solomon.”
Compare 2 Samuel 5:4–5 and 1 Kings 2:11, where David reigned seven years and six months in Hebron.
Hebrew “in the words of Samuel the seer.” These sources may be the books of Samuel or other prophetic records.
